title: Plans, Predictions & Future Forms
subtitle: Practise will and be going to through plans, evidence, and a realistic personal challenge.

sections.label: Lesson Notes
sections.title: What we explored
sections.intro: This lesson compared future forms and used them to talk about plans, decisions, predictions, and a short personal challenge.

cards.title: A plan already exists
cards.text: Use be going to when you have an intention or a plan made before the moment of speaking: “I’m going to start a new routine.”

cards.title: A decision now
cards.text: Use will for a decision made while speaking, an offer, or a simple prediction: “I’ll help you.”

cards.title: Look for evidence
cards.text: Be going to is also useful for a prediction with visible evidence: “That bag is too full. It’s going to break.”

sections.label: Grammar
sections.title: Will and be going to
sections.intro: Both forms can talk about the future, but the reason for choosing them is different.

cards.title: will + base verb
cards.text: Use will for an instant decision, offer, promise, or general prediction. Example: “The phone is ringing. I’ll answer it.”

cards.title: be going to + base verb
cards.text: Use am/is/are going to for a prior plan or evidence-based prediction. Example: “We’re going to meet friends; we arranged it last week.”

cards.title: Questions and negatives
cards.text: Will you join us? / I won’t forget. Are you going to study? / She isn’t going to travel.

cards.title: intention
cards.text: something you plan or want to do

cards.title: arrangement
cards.text: a plan made with another person

cards.title: evidence
cards.text: something that shows why you believe an idea is true

cards.title: commitment
cards.text: a serious promise to do something

cards.title: challenge
cards.text: a difficult task that can help you improve

cards.title: prediction
cards.text: a statement about what you think will happen

questions.q: The clouds are very dark. It ___ rain.
“I can’t carry these books.” “I ___ help you.”
questions.hint: This is an offer made now.

questions.q: We arranged it last week. We ___ meet on Saturday.
questions.hint: The plan existed before this moment.

readings.title: Three Weeks, One Clear Goal
readings.text:
Mina wants to make one small change over the next three weeks. She has chosen a simple goal: she is going to prepare a short English activity after dinner on four evenings each week. She is not planning to study for hours. Her plan is to spend fifteen minutes reading, listening, or reviewing a few words.

The plan is specific because Mina knows vague goals are difficult to follow. “I will improve my English” is a positive idea, but it does not say when or how. “I’m going to read for fifteen minutes after dinner” gives the action a place in the day. She has also told a friend about it, so the plan feels more like a commitment.

Mina knows that some days will be busy. A visitor may arrive, work may take longer than expected, or she may feel tired. She does not think every day will be perfect. However, she is going to return to the plan after a missed evening. A challenge is not useful because it creates pressure; it is useful because it helps a person notice what supports progress.

On the first Sunday, Mina looks at her notes. She can see that she completed three short activities, not four. She says, “Next week, I’ll prepare the reading before dinner.” This is a decision made at that moment. By changing one detail, she is making the plan easier to continue. The goal is not to create a perfect routine. It is to make a realistic promise and keep returning to it.

opt: It says when and how she will practise.
It asks her to study all day.
It has no connection to English.
questions.hint: Look at the first two paragraphs.

questions.q: What does Mina do after a missed evening?
questions.hint: The plan can continue after an interruption.

questions.q: Why does Mina say “I’ll prepare the reading before dinner”?
opt: It is an arrangement from last year.
It is a decision made while she is reviewing.

sections.label: Listening
sections.title: Listening follow-up
sections.intro: The lesson used listening about a short challenge. Use this routine with a brief English audio about plans or self-improvement.

cards.title: Before listening
cards.text: Predict: What challenge might the speaker choose? What future form might you hear?

cards.title: During listening
cards.text: Listen for one phrase with will and one phrase with going to. Decide whether each one is a plan, offer, decision, or prediction.

cards.title: After listening
cards.text: Say one sentence about your own next week: “I’ll …” or “I’m going to …” Explain why you chose that form.

questions.q: We bought the tickets yesterday. We ___ see the film on Friday.
